# Rainbow variant candidate validation

This hidden CI directory is not the production app. Root contains the actual candidate runtime, public catalog and unchanged production configuration. Never publish the disposable `.github/qa/fixture` or substitute synthetic data into root.

`verify-release.cjs` binds the candidate catalog and quote assets by SHA-256, checks all 3,469 original printing identities remain in the refreshed 3,505-card catalog, checks the original production configuration statement hashes without printing their values, and verifies v7 script/cache wiring, retained legacy keys and no forced service-worker takeover. The current production rollback reference is `6ef439a7a3ac59de0f273f484d4348b1800cd07d`; reverting code is not a data rollback.

`prepare-fixture.cjs` constructs a disposable localhost copy of these exact root runtime files. It replaces only cloud constants and catalog, adding synthetic tests/seeding; normalized app-source equality is asserted. No account, collection, login or live cloud data is read. The suite contains 95 unit/reference-model checks and 42 Chromium checks across desktop/mobile viewports, including a zero-owned public-catalog smoke test. Five unit checks cover a household reference model only, not a shipping household feature.

The database step runs pinned PostgreSQL and PostgREST containers on an internal Docker network. Its synthetic schema test verifies existing q/f/timestamps survive the additive rainbow column, old q/f merge-upserts and PATCH tombstones preserve rainbow quantities, compare-and-set guards reject stale writes, and owner/anonymous access isolation works. This is not a production schema execution or proof about every custom/old client.

The SQL under `.github/proposals` is an unapproved, deliberately aborting proposal, not an executable migration. Its rollout plan requires fresh private backup/snapshot, explicit approval, transactional preservation assertions, schema capability verification and reviewed deployment ordering. No migration, RLS, grants, auth, invitations or production data writes run in this workflow. Do not remove its guard and run it as a migration.

Runtime scope: distinct rainbow counts/controls, guarded manual sync, v6 local-state migration with legacy-change fencing, distinctly marked new backup/CSV formats, rainbow-preserving legacy restore, exact-finish valuation, 12 evidenced rainbow quotes, suppression of 13 ambiguous generic foil quotes, and 54 verified null-only market-ID mappings. The full overlay resolves 3,423 of 3,505 market links; 82 remain deliberately unresolved. Existing generic foil holdings are not relabeled cold foil. Quotes expire after seven days; missing/stale/mismatched quotes remain unpriced.

Browser tests block service workers, external traffic and production cloud requests. Physical camera recognition, actual phone hardware, Safari, authenticated production sync and offline/service-worker lifecycle are not verified. Existing old active workers may serve old assets until all old tabs/PWA instances close and the normal update activates. No forced cache or inventory clear is used.

This draft requires green CI, independent exact-source review and explicit production schema/deployment approval before merge. Pages is not deployed by this PR workflow. Legacy single-owner sync is not a transactional multi-phone household system. Old q/f clients cannot display or manage rainbow; custom DELETE/replace clients are outside compatibility guarantees. A legacy-change fence requires deliberate backup/reconciliation, not silent overwrite.
